transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-03
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Miguel Alvarez (Redwood AE), Priya Narang (Redwood SE), Lena Park (QoreOps), Markus Chen (QoreOps), Samir Rao (QoreOps)

Summary:
Quick walkthrough of Redwood's Usage Hub (per-route telemetry), cost attribution by route, and exportable billing breakdowns. Focus on economics for mixed hosted/dedicated deployment and how to run a short pilot. Q&A around data residency, KMS, and latency/cost tradeoffs.

Topics covered:
- Per-route dashboards and how routes are mapped to product features
- Token-level cost attribution and bucketed billing views
- Sampling, KV cache and batching effects on unit economics
- Private/Dedicated routing options and audit logs

Transcript body:
[00:00] Miguel Alvarez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — this is Miguel from Redwood. We got Priya on the seads -> the seads is (laugh) the SE side to walk through the Usage Hub.
[00:18] Lena Park: Hi, thanks. We just have a short agenda, mostly want to see how per-feature routes map to cost. Our finance team keeps asking why some endpoints spike.
[00:25] Priya Narang: Great, we'll start with the route map. Quick note — some auto transcription will call our product "Redwood Consol" in the text sometimes, so apologies if there's a mismatch in the recording.
[00:37] Markus Chen: No problem. Also for context we run a hybrid: some models on dedicated GPU pools and some on hosted. We care about per-route p99 latency and per-token cost.
[00:48] Samir Rao: And we need exportable reports for our chargeback system, CSV or S3 preferred.
[00:54] Miguel Alvarez: Perfect. I'll share my screen — starting with the Routes overview in the Usage Hub. You can map routes to tags, services, or product feature names. Each route shows tokens in, tokens out, cache hits, and per-model cost estimate.
[01:10] Priya Narang: (screen) So here's an example route called "inference/chat/recommend" — you can see the token distribution histogram, latency percentiles, and a cost bar split by model variant. The cost model uses per-token rates combined with measured batching and KV cache efficiency.
[01:28] Lena Park: Can we override rates? Our procurement has negotiated model rates with a cloud provider — we need to reflect that.
[01:33] Priya Narang: Yes, you can set custom rate profiles per account or per-route. We also support bucketing for committed capacity to show committed vs on-demand unit economics.
[01:45] Markus Chen: How granular are the attributions? We have composite features that fan-out to three routes per request.
[01:51] Miguel Alvarez: Good question. Attribution is additive by token counts across downstream routes. We show path-level traces so you can see the fan-out and how tokens are attributed across sub-routes. There's also a path sampling mode to limit overhead.
[02:05] Samir Rao: Sampling mode — what's the error profile there? We can't have billing variances that upset finance.
[02:11] Priya Narang: Sampling is configurable; the default is 1% sample for heavy routes, and we provide confidence intervals on the estimated chargeback. For billing-critical reports you can enable deterministic mode which records every token but it will increase cost and storage.
[02:28] Lena Park: Ok. And for private deployments — our security team will insist on KMS/HSM and audit logs. How does Redwood handle that?
[02:35] Miguel Alvarez: For Private you get customer-managed KMS integrations, audit log retention options, and optional air-gapped on-prem packages. We also offer a hardened control plane that keeps metadata in your VPC.
[02:48] Markus Chen: Is there an SLA difference if we go mixed model? We want dedicated pools for low-latency paths but host smaller models.
[02:56] Miguel Alvarez: Dedicated pools have SLA-backed latency targets and predictable throughput. Hosted has elasticity and lower upfront commitment. The platform can route by policy — latency-sensitive routes to dedicated, cost-sensitive to hosted, and fallback rules if capacity's constrained.
[03:12] Samir Rao: Does Redwood surface the cost delta of moving a route to dedicated?
[03:15] Priya Narang: Yes, the Optimize tab computes estimated TCO over time. It factors in reserved capacity discounts, average utilization, and expected batching effects. We can run a "what-if" simulation for your traffic patterns.
[03:27] Lena Park: Can you run that simulation in the pilot?
[03:29] Miguel Alvarez: Absolutely. For the pilot we'll ingest a week's worth of route-level traffic from you and run cost-sensitivity sims.
[03:34] Markus Chen: On instrumentation — how do we tag routes? We already have a pattern: service:feature:env in our headers.
[03:40] Priya Narang: Great, Redwood can map headers to route names automatically. We also expose an API to create routes and tags programmatically.
[03:47] Lena Park: Let's talk about latency vs batching. We saw earlier that batching helps cost but increases tail latency.
[03:53] Priya Narang: Right. Our continuous batching is workload aware — it attempts micro-batches within configured latency SLOs. For chat UIs we usually keep max latency 50-100ms; for offline generation you can push larger batches. The Usage Hub shows cost/latency tradeoff curves per route.
[04:08] Markus Chen: Can we run A/B tests to measure user impact after changing model variants or batching settings?
[04:11] Miguel Alvarez: Yes, rollouts support canary and A/B with automatic rollback on quality regressions. We tie to eval sets so you can monitor semantic drift.
[04:20] Samir Rao: About billing exports — we need daily files to S3 with per-route spend. Is that possible?
[04:25] Priya Narang: Yes, daily exports to S3, Snowflake connectors, or direct CSV download. We can also push webhook events for large anomalies.
[04:33] Lena Park: Will metadata like team and cost center be included?
[04:36] Miguel Alvarez: You can include arbitrary tags and customer-managed metadata. We include token-level attribution mapped to those tags.
[04:44] Markus Chen: Any limitations if we use on-prem bouts — I mean on-prem instance?
[04:49] Priya Narang: On-prem has the same telemetry but you host storage for logs; you can choose to forward aggregates to Redwood control plane or keep everything internal.
[04:58] Lena Park: Are there pre-built dashboards for compliance audits?
[05:01] Priya Narang: We have audit dashboards and canned reports for SOC2 and ISO; you'll get exportable timelines and access logs with user-level RBAC filters.
[05:10] (brief crosstalk)
[05:20] Miguel Alvarez: Ok walking through a sample route detail. Notice the per-day cost heatmap. This is where you can click a spike and get a trace waterfall showing the fan-out and the token counts per child route.
[05:36] Markus Chen: That waterfall would be huge for some of our spikes. Does Redwood store full traces by default?
[05:41] Priya Narang: We sample traces by default; full tracing is optional. For pilot we can enable dense traces for 48 hours to capture a representative spike.
[05:50] Lena Park: About the charges for dense tracing — is that tracked separately?
[05:54] Miguel Alvarez: Yes, tracing and storage are billed separately or can be included in a pilot credit. We'll call that out in the pricing sheet.
[06:04] Samir Rao: One of our concerns is misattribution when models are quantized — do unit costs reflect quantized model performance?
[06:11] Priya Narang: The platform supports quantization profiles. Costs reflect measured throughput and latency for the quantized variant; the lookup table uses benchmarks we run in our runtime. There can be small measurement jitter but we surface calibration guides.
[06:25] Markus Chen: Competitor question — ModelServeX had an "aggregated route" concept that rolled everything up. How is Redwood different?
[06:32] Miguel Alvarez: We do both aggregated views and fine-grained per-path traces. Our difference is the Optimize module that provides prescriptive actions: "move route X to dedicated pool" or "enable KV cache on route Y" with an estimated ROI.
[06:47] Lena Park: ROI calc — is that per month or 90-day?
[06:50] Priya Narang: You can choose the horizon: 30/90/365 days.
[06:53] (silence)
[07:00] Markus Chen: Ok curious about keys, encryption, and multi-tenant isolation.
[07:04] Miguel Alvarez: For hosted we encrypt data at rest and in transit; we support customer-managed KMS and tenant isolation features. For Dedicated and Private you get stronger network isolation and optional HSM.
[07:17] Lena Park: Our compliance team also wants proof of key rotation policies.
[07:21] Priya Narang: We have rotation logs that can be exported; we'll include our KMS architecture doc in the follow-up.
[07:29] Miguel Alvarez: Quick demo of the Cost Breakdown page. Here you can filter by tag, route, model, and date range. The chart shows total spend, unit cost, and an efficiency metric (tokens per $).
[07:44] Samir Rao: Nice, tokens per dollar is handy. Can you compute cost per converted user? We have a metric for LTV tied to feature calls.
[07:50] Priya Narang: You can map events from your analytics to routes and compute cost per event; we also have an API to export per-route cost to a BI tool where you can join with conversion metrics.
[08:02] Lena Park: For pilot sizing, what's the minimum committed capacity if we want dedicated for one route?
[08:07] Miguel Alvarez: Depends on model size. For a small 8B variant you'd need a single reserved GPU cluster — typical customers commit to a full pool or use burst capacity. We'll put exact numbers in pricing.
[08:21] Markus Chen: Can the Usage Hub flag anomalies proactively?
[08:24] Priya Narang: Anomaly detection is built-in; you can set thresholds by route or let the system pick baselines. We send alerts and can create auto-runbooks or open a ticket in your ops tool.
[08:36] Lena Park: We have an internal FinOps workflow that requires triage and owner assignment. Can alerts be routed to owners?
[08:41] Miguel Alvarez: Yes, integrate with Slack, PagerDuty, Jira and assign owners automatically.
[08:47] (a few seconds of typing/noise)
[09:02] Samir Rao: Ok, this is helpful. Could you walk us through the pilot scope so we know the deliverables?
[09:08] Miguel Alvarez: Pilot scope: ingest 7 days of route-level traffic, enable dense tracing for 48h on spike windows, run cost-sensitivity sims, and deliver a pilot report with recommended route placements and expected savings.
[09:21] Priya Narang: We'll also instrument two example routes with KV cache and batching tweaks so you can see delta in a controlled environment.
[09:30] Lena Park: Sounds good. Timeline?
[09:33] Miguel Alvarez: If you can provide route CSV by Aug 10, we can start pilot on Aug 17 and deliver results by Aug 28.
[09:41] Markus Chen: Who signs the NDA or do we need a PO?
[09:44] Miguel Alvarez: For pilot we usually do a standard trial agreement; for procurement we'll share our order form. I'll send legal contacts in the follow-up.
[09:53] (brief pause)
[10:05] Lena Park: Can Redwood show token-level distribution for anonymized PII concerns? We need to ensure redaction.
[10:12] Priya Narang: We support automatic PII redaction and field-level hashing. For Private deployments you can keep raw data in your VPC.
[10:21] Miguel Alvarez: We're nearing time — last items: export formats, billing cadence, and pilot credit.
[10:28] Priya Narang: Billing can be daily or monthly; pilot credit depends on scope, we'll include a credit line for the tracing window.
[10:36] Lena Park: Great. Any blockers we might hit with our security team?
[10:39] Miguel Alvarez: The usual: keys, network peering, and legal review. We have templates and an onboarding playbook.
[10:47] Markus Chen: Ok let's recap next steps.
[10:50] Miguel Alvarez: Recap — Miguel to send pricing, KMS diagram, and pilot template; Priya to prepare the runbook and trace script; Markus to provide route CSV; Lena to loop in security; Samir to review cost allocations with finance.
[11:05] Samir Rao: I'll coordinate with finance; thanks.
[11:08] Lena Park: Thanks everyone.
[11:10] Miguel Alvarez: Thanks, we'll follow up by email with dates and the pilot kickoff.

End of transcript.
